concepts.name: Combining groups
concepts.description: The combined average is the total of all values divided by the total count, so each group counts by its size.

concepts.name: The seesaw: sizes from averages
concepts.description: The combined average sits between the group averages, closer to the larger group; the distances give the size ratio.

concepts.name: Members joining or leaving
concepts.description: Track totals, not averages: a change in one value shifts the total by exactly that amount.

concepts.name: Time and other weights
concepts.description: Averages of rates such as speed are weighted by time (or by distance for the reciprocal).

formulas.title: Combined average
formulas.prompt: Group 1 has n₁ members with average a₁ and group 2 has n₂ with average a₂. What is the combined average?
formulas.explanation: Each group's total is its size times its average. Add the totals, then divide by the total number.
formulas.applicationPrompt: 10 boys average 40 kg and 15 girls average 30 kg. What is the average weight of all 25?

formulas.title: Seesaw (alligation) rule
formulas.prompt: A mixed group has average C and its two parts have averages a₁ < C < a₂. What is the ratio of their sizes?
formulas.explanation: The group with the smaller distance to C has more members, because it pulls the average harder.
formulas.commonMistake: Putting the distances the wrong way round.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A class averages 68. Boys average 65 and girls average 72. What is the ratio of boys to girls?

formulas.title: Totals track changes
formulas.prompt: One member joins or leaves a group. How do you find that member's value?
formulas.formula:
Total = Average × Count
Joiner = New total − Old total
Leaver = Old total − New total
formulas.explanation: Averages cannot be added or subtracted, but totals can. Always convert to totals first.
formulas.example:
8 numbers average 15 → total 120
A 9th number 24 → total 144 → new average 16
formulas.commonMistake: Adding or subtracting the averages themselves.
formulas.applicationPrompt: The average of 30 students is 14. With the teacher included it is 15. How old is the teacher?

formulas.title: Weighted by time
formulas.prompt: A trip has legs at different speeds. How do you find the average speed?
formulas.formula: Average speed = Total distance ÷ Total time
formulas.explanation: Speed is distance per unit time, so the average is weighted by time. Equal times give the simple mean; equal distances give the harmonic form.
formulas.example:
60 km at 40 km/hr (1.5 hr) and 90 km at 60 km/hr (1.5 hr)
150 ÷ 3 = 50 km/hr
formulas.commonMistake: Averaging the two speeds when the times are not equal.
formulas.applicationPrompt: A train covers 60 km at 40 km/hr and 90 km at 60 km/hr. What is its average speed?

formulas.title: Value of the one who leaves
formulas.prompt: One of n members leaves and the average changes from A to B. What was the leaver's value?
formulas.explanation: The old total minus the new total is exactly what left.
formulas.example: 10 members average 30; one leaves and the average falls to 29: 300 − 261 = 39.
formulas.commonMistake: Using n for the new group as well.
formulas.applicationPrompt: The average age of 25 students is 15; when the teacher is included it rises by 1. Find the teacher's age.

levels.title: Bigger Groups Pull Harder
levels.description: Why the average of two averages is usually wrong, and what to do instead.

blocks.title: Do not average the averages
blocks.body: If 20 students average 60 and 30 average 70, the class average is not 65. The bigger group pulls the combined average towards itself. The right answer comes from totals: (1,200 + 2,100) ÷ 50 = 66.

blocks.title: Combined average
blocks.caption: Each average counts as many times as its group has members.

blocks.title: The seesaw
blocks.body: The combined average always sits between the two group averages, and closer to the larger group. The distances tell you the size ratio: the group nearer the mean is the bigger one, in the inverse ratio of the distances.

levels.title: Weighted Average Formulas
levels.description: Combined averages, the seesaw rule, totals and weights.

levels.title: Direct Weighted Averages
levels.description: Combine two groups and add one member.

questions.question: 20 students score an average of 60 and another 30 students score an average of 70. What is the average score of all 50?
questions.explanation: Totals: 20 × 60 = 1,200 and 30 × 70 = 2,100. Combined = 3,300 ÷ 50 = 66. It is closer to 70 because the larger group scored 70.
questions.method: Weight each average by its group size.

hints.text: The groups are different sizes, so the simple average 65 is not right.

questions.question: 10 boys have an average weight of 40 kg and 15 girls have an average weight of 30 kg. What is the average weight of all 25 children, in kg?
questions.method: Total of all ÷ number of all.

hints.text: Convert each group into a total weight.

questions.question: 25 men have an average score of 80 and 25 women have an average score of 60. What is the average of all 50?
questions.explanation: The groups are the same size, so the combined average is exactly halfway: (80 + 60) ÷ 2 = 70. Check with totals: (2,000 + 1,500) ÷ 50 = 70.
solutionSteps: Equal group sizes → the simple average works.
questions.method: Equal sizes make the weighted average equal the simple one.

hints.text: How do the two group sizes compare?

questions.question: A group of n₁ items has average a₁ and another group of n₂ items has average a₂. The average of all the items together is
questions.explanation: n₁a₁ and n₂a₂ are the two totals. Divide the grand total by the total number of items.
questions.method: Weight each average by its size.

hints.text: Which option gives more influence to the bigger group?

questions.question: The average of 8 numbers is 15. A 9th number, 24, is added. What is the new average?
questions.explanation: Old total = 8 × 15 = 120. New total = 120 + 24 = 144. New average = 144 ÷ 9 = 16.

questions.question: The average age of 30 students is 14 years. When the teacher's age is included, the average becomes 15. How old is the teacher, in years?
questions.explanation: Total with teacher = 31 × 15 = 465. Total of students = 30 × 14 = 420. Teacher = 465 − 420 = 45.
questions.method: New total − old total = the joiner.

hints.text: Count the teacher when finding the new total.

commonMistakes: Using 30 members for the new total.

questions.question: The average mark of a class is 68. The girls average 72 and the boys average 65. What is the ratio of girls to boys?
questions.explanation: Distances from 68: girls are 4 away, boys are 3 away. The ratio of girls : boys is the distance of the OTHER group over this one's: (68 − 65) : (72 − 68) = 3 : 4. The boys, being closer to 68, are the larger group.
solutionSteps: Boys are 3 below the average; girls are 4 above.
questions.method: The closer group has more members.

hints.text: The nearer group is the bigger one.

commonMistakes: Putting the distances the wrong way round (4 : 3).

questions.question: The average of 6 numbers is 20. When one number is removed, the average of the remaining 5 is 18. What is the number removed?
questions.explanation: Total of 6 = 120. Total of remaining 5 = 90. Removed number = 120 − 90 = 30.
questions.method: Old total − new total = the leaver.

questions.question: The average of 50 numbers is 38. Two numbers, 45 and 55, are discarded. What is the average of the remaining numbers?
questions.explanation: Total = 50 × 38 = 1,900. After removing 45 + 55 = 100, the total is 1,800 for 48 numbers. 1,800 ÷ 48 = 37.5.
questions.method: Adjust the total and the count.

hints.text: What are the new total and the new count?

commonMistakes: Leaving the average at 38 because 45 and 55 average 50.

questions.question: A batsman's average after his 12th innings is 48, which is 2 more than his average after 11 innings. How many runs did he score in the 12th innings?
questions.explanation: Before: 11 × 46 = 506 runs. After: 12 × 48 = 576 runs. The 12th innings = 576 − 506 = 70.

hints.text: What was the average before the 12th innings?

questions.question: A train travels the first 60 km at 40 km/hr and the next 90 km at 60 km/hr. What is its average speed for the whole journey, in km/hr?
questions.explanation: Time for the first part = 60 ÷ 40 = 1.5 hr, for the second = 90 ÷ 60 = 1.5 hr. Total time = 3 hr for 150 km, so the average is 50 km/hr.
solutionSteps: Total distance 150 km, total time 3 hr.
questions.method: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time.

hints.text: Find how long each part takes.

questions.question: Three groups of 10, 20 and 30 people have averages of 30, 45 and x respectively. The average of all 60 people is 50. What is x?
questions.explanation: Total of all = 60 × 50 = 3,000. Groups 1 and 2 contribute 300 + 900 = 1,200. So group 3's total is 1,800 and x = 1,800 ÷ 30 = 60.
questions.method: Subtract known totals from the grand total.

hints.text: What does group 3 have to add up to?

commonMistakes: Solving with averages instead of totals.

questions.question: The average salary of all 90 employees of a firm is ₹8,000. Officers average ₹12,000 and other staff average ₹6,000. How many officers are there?
questions.explanation: Distances from 8,000: officers 4,000 above, others 2,000 below. Officers : others = 2,000 : 4,000 = 1 : 2, so officers are 1/3 of 90 = 30.
solutionSteps: Others are 2,000 from the mean; officers are 4,000 from it.
commonMistakes: Inverting the ratio to get 60 officers.
